newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - BTP call spreads snapped up amid bull run.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - BTP call spreads snapped up amid bull run.

text.p: BTP call spreads were in demand on Tuesday as the underlying futures took off once again and reached record highs, dealers said.
December BTP futures on LIFFE surged to an all-time high of 126.55 on Tuesday, although by 1450 GMT they had drifted back to 126.18, still 53 basis points higher on the day.
"We're seeing the same sort of thing that we were seeing in earlier rallies in BTPs -- a lot of call spreads in both December and March," said a trader at an Italian bank in London.

"They believe in the rally but there's got to be a limit. As far as volatility is conerned it's pretty much as it was. We haven't seen vol bid up on the back of this move. It was pretty high before and it's staying pretty constant," he added.
Call spreads involve buying calls at one strike and selling them at strikes further out of the money. If the rally does not go far beyond the more distant strike, the investor makes money.

A trader said one player had been buying 127.00 BTP calls and selling 128.00 calls in a one-by-two ratio. In this particular trade the client paid nine ticks, resulting in a cost of 180 million lire for 1,000 contracts. Each BTP contract is for 200 million lire in nominal value.
The trader said the breakeven point was 129.00 and if the market rallied further the trade would lose money.
The maximum payout, if the market reached 128.00 by expiry on November 21, was two billion lire, he said.
Another London dealer said there had been a 5,000-contract December 128.00-129.00 call spread, although with December options so near expiry, he said March strategies made more sense.
He said banks had been putting on one-by-two March call spreads at 129.00-131.00 and at 128.00-130.00 strikes.
But there were risks in such strategies, especially as BTPs had a habit of making sudden large leaps, dealers said.

"Granted it's 3-1/2 points away from the market but the danger with these one-by-twos is you get smacked," one dealer said. "You find you're okay at 129.00 to 130.00 but from 130.00 on they really start to work against you."
Dealers said international interest in BTP options is on the rise, with U.S. hedge funds and others taking part, boosting volume levels on LIFFE for BTP contracts to new highs.
The trader at the Italian bank said December volatility was around 9.3 percent, while March was around eight percent, both little changed from levels on Monday.
